# Radoslav Radev Advises Five Minutes Rest Between Planche Attempts And A Six-Attempt Maximum

Radoslav Radev says you are ready with six attempts maximum. He says to rest five minutes between them, or do four attempts. [src: vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 02:56]

## Details

- Radev says the first attempt is good, the second is good, the third is good, and the fourth, fifth, and sixth attempts become worse. [src: vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 02:24]
- He says that after many attempts, the next workout can find you without strength because your nervous system is too tired. [src: vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 02:44]
- Radev says you are ready with six attempts maximum. [src: vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 02:56]
- He says to rest five minutes between attempts, or do four attempts. [src: vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 02:56]
- He says you do not need 10 attempts. [src: vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 03:17]
- He also says you do not need 15 attempts. [src: vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 03:17]
- After holding a lower progression as much as you can, he says you can end up with one productive workout for the week or for the month. [src: vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 03:17]

## Evidence

- vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 02:24 (Radoslav Radev): "you're not putting resistance band to fix your technique or always you're trying to do more and more seconds and you see how first attempt is good second is good the third is good but the fourth fifth one sixth one they go they becoming worse"
- vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 02:44 (Radoslav Radev): "you reach maximum and you tire it yourself a lot and the next workout you have no strength and even if you rest also you have no power because your nervous system is too tired"
- vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 02:56 (Radoslav Radev): "you're ready with six attempts maximum ... five minutes rest between them or four attempts"
- vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 03:17 (Radoslav Radev): "i mean you don't need to do 10 attempts 15 attempts"
- vid-z_gI3IGFwCY @ 03:17 (Radoslav Radev): "go on a lower progression hold maximum as you can tire your nervous system and you end up with one productive workout for the week or for the month"
